title: The Concept of Wave-Particle Duality
text:
Quantum mechanics dictates that matter exhibits characteristics of both waves and particles, a principle known as wave-particle duality. This means entities such as photons and electrons do not exclusively adopt one form but rather display properties depending on the experimental setup used for observation.

The double-slit experiment remains the foundational demonstration of this concept. When observed in intervals, electrons act like discrete points (particles); however, when passing through two slits without measurement, they produce an interference pattern characteristic only of waves. This dual nature challenges classical understanding and necessitates a probabilistic interpretation of reality.
